notes: Thirteen labels, all 'Sr. X. –' with an en dash. The chair is printed with no surname at all ('Sr. Presidente. –'), as the brief says is usual before 2016; I did not supply 'Pampuro' or any other name. Each numbered section heading is printed as a centred number on its own line above a centred all-caps title; I joined the two the way the format example joins them ('6. Asuntos entrados'), so '1. IZAMIENTO DE LA BANDERA NACIONAL' stands for two printed lines. Rule 2 matters a lot here: the chair speaks nine times and five of those turns are separated from the previous one only by a heading or a stenographer note, and each is listed. Two unlabelled indented paragraphs reading 'Tiene la palabra el señor senador Pichetto.' (after the artículo 1º turn and after the artículo 58 turn) are run-ons of the chair's own turn, not new starts. The third turn ends 'esta sesión preparatoria.2' — that 2 is the footnote pointer for 'Ver el Apéndice.' at the foot, so it is out of first_words and the footnote line is under furniture. The (Aplausos.) in the flag-raising note is inside that note's own paragraph, so it stays part of the event rather than becoming one. TYPOGRAPHY: the Morales paragraph is the only one on the page set ragged-right instead of justified — its first line breaks early after 'para la' and the rest is unjustified, which looks like a formatting accident in the original.
